D.t: Lynne Walz trails by 1.7 and wins 38% of simulations. Closing it takes about 6,550 voters switching sides, or 13,100 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +8.2 and D +4.9. A normal polling error decides it.

The polls page average is R +2.3. Your best recent poll is Concord Public Opinion Partners for Education Reform Now Advocacy (D) at D +0.3; your worst is Echelon Insights for NetChoice (R) at R +7.3. 9 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Douglas, a projected net 69,294 votes; Lancaster, a projected net 34,622 votes; Sarpy, a projected net 7,948 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Sarpy, D +10.2, 10.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Lynne Walz runs furthest behind in Platte, Madison, Washington. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 90% of voters, 44 to 50, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.50 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 70% of voters, 45 to 49, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.48 points; Voters without a degree, 60% of voters, 43 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.98 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Lynne Walz: Immigration voters 21 to 73, Small counties 28 to 65, Incomes $125K and up 39 to 55. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$860K cash against $7.5M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
Registered Democrats cast 39% of the 215,424 ballots in Nebraska so far, against 44% for the other party. That is 4.2 points better for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.3 points toward Lynne Walz. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.
Cash: $7.5M in the bank against $860K for Lynne Walz.

R.t: Jim Pillen leads by 1.7 in the forecast and wins 62% of simulations. The cushion is about 13,100 votes; a one point swing is about 3,876 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +4.9 and R +8.2. A normal polling error decides it.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Platte, a projected net 6,992 votes; Madison, a projected net 6,112 votes; Lincoln, a projected net 4,513 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Sarpy, D +10.2, 10.0% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Jim Pillen runs furthest behind in Lincoln, Lancaster, Sarpy. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 90% of voters, 50 to 44, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.50 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 70% of voters, 49 to 45, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.48 points; Voters without a degree, 60% of voters, 51 to 43, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.98 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Jim Pillen: Independents 20 to 69, 2024 nonvoters and third party voters 28 to 64, Moderates 28 to 64. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$7.5M cash against $860K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
